en: Of course, in order to use Ollama, you need
to download and install it. And you can
visit ollama.com,
and then there you'll find a download
button. And as you see, it is available for
macOS, Linux, and Windows.
And just like LM Studio, you can use it on
all these platforms to run all kinds of AI
models on these platforms, no matter if you
have high-end hardware or if you're more on
the lower end.
So that's just the same as with LM Studio,
but unlike LM Studio, as you'll see, Ollama
does not come with a graphical user
interface, but I'll get back to that.
So let's download Ollama. Here I'm on macOS,
so I will download this version.
And once the download finished, you can walk
through the installer or on macOS, simply
drag and drop the extracted Ollama
application file into your Applications
folder.
And then you can just start Ollama.
Now, as mentioned, it doesn't come with any
graphical user interface. So the only
indication I got here on macOS telling me
that it's running
is this indicator here in my status bar.
On Windows, you should find Ollama in your
system tray.
And you can check whether Ollama was
installed or not by opening your terminal,
your command line on your system, the one
that's built into your system.
And then there you should run the Ollama
command. And that's a command that should be
available if Ollama was installed
successfully.
If that fails, if that command is not found,
try restarting your terminal or system. And
of course, make sure that you did
successfully walk through that Ollama
installer
or drag and drop it into the Applications
folder on macOS and that you did start
Ollama after installing it and then try
again.
Ultimately, you should get some output like
this, which proves that Ollama was installed
successfully. So the next question of course
is how we can use Ollama on our system.
